DomainError.ts defines the shared abstraction, which is the abstract base class DomainError with an abstract `kind: DomainErrorKind` and a protected constructor that sets `name`. The other four errors (NotFoundError, TaskAlreadyDoneError, UnknownAssigneeError, ValidationError) all extend that base the same way. Each one sets a literal `kind` from the shared DomainErrorKind union and builds its message only through `super(...)`. The `kind` union and the naming rule (`this.name = new.target.name`) are each defined only once, in DomainError.ts, so no rule is duplicated. No subclass sets `name` again or skips the base constructor, so none of them bypasses the module's abstraction. Both UnknownAssigneeError and ValidationError use kind 'validation'. That is a shared category, not a duplicated rule. UnknownAssigneeError adds a more specific message, which is a valid domain distinction.
